text:
sai: Quick heads-up — after we flipped the kernel-selector to v2 yesterday, I noticed a tail in queue wait on the long-seq routes ( >1024 ). Posting some quick notes and a couple of PromQL queries I used.

maria: Can you share the exact symptom? p50/p95/p99 changes?

sai: p50 roughly same, p95 up ~18ms, p99 up ~120ms for route /generate-long. Token-level breakdown shows most added time is in 'queue_wait' and 'first_token_kernel'.

jonathan: Do you have batch-size histograms? wondering if v2 interacts strangely with small-batch fast paths.

sai: Yep. Batch size shifted left a bit — spike in 1-2 token batches on that route. Likely because our new kernel heuristic picks a smaller micro-kernel for shorter sequences, but when long seqs come in they sometimes get split oddly by the scheduler.

ash: (ops note) Perf alert fired at 02:13 UTC: perf-regression /generate-long p99 > baseline+100ms :eyes:

perf-bot: [ALERT] perf-regression: route=/generate-long p99=412ms (baseline=285ms) — triggered at 2026-11-05T02:13:18Z

maria: Can we get the KV cache hit/miss around the same time? If a bunch of cold KV misses happen, that would inflate queue wait and kernel overhead.

jonathan: I ran a small profiler dump during the spike. Snippet:

```
# condensed trace sample
[2026-11-05T02:12:57Z] request id=abc123 route=/generate-long seq=2048
  scheduler.enqueue_wait=89ms
  batch_build=6ms
  kvcache.lookup=14ms (miss)
  kernel_compile_path=v2_micro
  kernel_exec=210ms
  total_server=330ms
```

ash: kvcache.lookup miss latency 14ms seems high — might be falling back to storage. What's our miss rate trend?

sai: Miss rate jumped from 2.1% -> 7.9% for that tenant during the incident window. I suspect cache eviction churn because v2 changed kernel memory layout and slightly increased per-request KV memory, bumping the LRU.

maria: Proposed immediate actions: 1) revert selector to v1 on dedicated pools hitting p99 regressions, 2) add a temporary alert on batch_size_p50<3 && p99>baseline+50ms, 3) add panel for kvcache_eviction_rate by tenant.

jonathan: For observability, I added two Grafana panels drafts:

- "batch_size_vs_queue_wait heatmap" using this PromQL: 
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
```
- "token-latency-waterfall" which breaks down per-token labels: queue_wait, kv_lookup, kernel_first_token, kernel_subsequent_tokens.
```
sum by (route,token_phase) (rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m]))
```

ash: small nit: histogram_quantile on batch_size_bucket might be noisy; recommend using count_over_time to compute median batch size instead for alerting.

sai: Also attaching quick dashboard sketch (pasted):
```
panels:
- id: 101
  title: "Per-route token latency waterfall"
  queries:
    - expr: 'sum by (route, phase) (rate(token_latency_seconds_sum[5m])) / sum by (route, phase) (rate(token_latency_seconds_count[5m]))'
- id: 102
  title: "Batch size histogram (5m)"
  queries:
    - expr: 'histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))'
- id: 103
  title: "KV cache eviction rate"
  queries:
    - expr: 'sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m])) by (tenant)'
```

maria: That looks fine for a quick iteration. For long-term, we should also surface scheduler efficiency: fraction of batches that hit target size vs actual size.

jonathan: I can add a metric: scheduler.effective_batch_ratio = actual_batch_size / target_batch_size. Query idea: 
```
sum(rate(scheduler_actual_batch_size_sum[5m])) / sum(rate(scheduler_target_batch_size_sum[5m]))
```

perf-bot: [INFO] rollbacks: no auto-rollback configured for kernel-selector flips on prod.

ash: Given tenant-specific KV churn, I'm +1 to revert selector v2 for the affected pool and then run A/B with pinned kvcache capacity + slightly higher cache RPO.

sai: I'll open a quick rollback PR and add the temporary heatmap + eviction panel. Also will instrument scheduler.effective_batch_ratio and a per-route kernel-choice breakdown.

maria: Can you also add a dashboard annotation for the exact flip time so we can correlate? date: 2026-11-05T02:11:00Z

sai: Will do. Next steps:
- rollback kernel-selector v2 on pool-12 (sai)
- add panels and alert (jonathan)
- bump kvcache capacity for pool-12 by +15% (ops ticket)

jonathan: I can have the panels and queries ready in ~45m, will post links.

maria: Thanks — please ping #eng-runtime when rollback is done so we can watch metrics. :thumbsup:

sai: rollback in progress, will update in thread when completed. :mechanical_arm:
